title: Technology Sector Update for 07/06/2018: FB,RSYS,SATS - Nasdaq.com
text:

Tech stocks were falling ahead of Friday's opening bell.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Facebook ( FB ) was slightly lower in early Friday trading, slipping just 0.1%, after the social networking company reportedly is in talks for what could be its biggest original series yet, a docu-series on soccer superstar Cristiano Ronaldo for Facebook Watch, Variety wrote late Thursday, citing sources. Facebook is ready to shell out plenty of money on the project, with Ronaldo reportedly earning around $10 million for the 13-episode show. Ronaldo has been the most popular athlete on Facebook with more than 120 million followers on his official page.
In other sector news:
- RadiSys ( RSYS ) retreated in Thursday's after-market, falling over 1%, after the telecommunications software and equipment company said it temporarily has fallen out of compliance with Nasdaq Stock Market rules requiring listed companies to have at least three members on its board audit committee following the resignation of board member Niel Ransom. The company expects to name a replacement and regain compliance by its next shareholders annual meeting or within one year of the resignation, whichever is sooner.
= Echostar ( SATS ) was unchanged in early Friday trading, with the satellite communications company reportedly seeking constructive talks with the Inmarsat board of directors after the UK-based company rebuffed its latest takeover offer worth GBP3.2 billion, or about $4.2 billion. Echostar's increased July 3 bid was a mixture of cash and stock totaling 5.32 pence for each Inmarsat share. The British firm rejected its initial bid back in June, saying that the proposal significantly undervalued the company. Echostar has until 1700 local, or 12 pm ET, on Friday to update its bid.
